Class Limelight

java.lang.Object
frc.spectrumLib.vision.Limelight
public class Limelight extends Object
Provides a high-level interface to a single Limelight camera for AprilTag-based pose estimation and basic targeting.

All methods are safe to call when the camera is not attached (isAttached() returns false); they return zero / false / empty values in that case.

NetworkTables reads are snapshotted per robot loop: the first getter to need a topic reads it once and every later getter in the same loop reuses that sample, so pose, tag count, raw fiducials and timestamp always describe the same camera frame. The owning subsystem must call invalidate() exactly once per loop before any getter. Returned LimelightHelpers.PoseEstimate and LimelightHelpers.RawFiducial instances are shared for the rest of the loop and must not be mutated.

Two pose estimation flavors are supported:

  • MegaTag1 is full 3-D pose estimation using one or more AprilTags.
  • MegaTag2 is a fused estimate that incorporates the robot heading supplied via setRobotOrientation(double).

    • invalidate

      public void invalidate()
      Clears the per-loop NetworkTables snapshot so the next getter re-reads the camera.

      Must be called exactly once per robot loop, before any pose/target getter, by the owning subsystem (see Vision.periodic()). Between calls, every getter on this object returns data from the same NetworkTables sample. Safe to call on a detached camera.

    • pushConfiguredCameraPose

      public void pushConfiguredCameraPose()
      Writes this camera's configured mount pose (Limelight.LimelightConfig.withTranslation(double, double, double) and Limelight.LimelightConfig.withRotation(double, double, double)) to the camera over NetworkTables, making the code the source of truth for the offsets instead of the values typed into the web UI.

      The six values are stored in exactly the convention the camera wants: forward, right, up in metres, then roll, pitch, yaw in degrees. They go across unchanged. That is the same order and sign as the boxes in the web UI, so what is in VisionConfig can be read straight off against what a camera is showing.

      A Limelight keeps its own copy in flash and falls back to it on boot, so this has to be republished rather than written once: a camera that reboots mid-match otherwise silently reverts to whatever was last typed into it. See the resend loop in Vision.periodic().

      Does not flush NetworkTables; the caller flushes once after all per-loop writes.

    • setRobotOrientation

      public void setRobotOrientation(double degrees, double angularRate)
      Sets the robot orientation and yaw rate for the Limelight's internal IMU fusion (MegaTag2).

      Does not flush NetworkTables; the caller is responsible for a single flush after all per-loop writes (see Vision.periodic()).

      Parameters:
      degrees - robot heading in degrees (positive counter-clockwise)
      angularRate - current yaw rate in degrees per second
